title: Bay rum aftershave splash
subtitle: A traditional spiced alcohol tonic for after shaving
excerpt: Bay rum aftershave is a traditional alcohol-based post-shave tonic made by steeping dried bay leaves and allspice berries in high-strength vodka or isopropyl alcohol, then diluting with witch hazel and water. The result is a spiced, warm splash that cools and firms the skin after shaving. One batch makes 200 ml; infuse for two to four weeks before filtering.
sourceNotes: Bay rum tradition: documented in Henry Clapp Baker, Ship Chandlery and Ships' Supplies (1897) and The Barbershop Blue Book (2018, historical compilation). Original bay rum was made from West Indian bay leaf (Pimenta racemosa) and rum; modern recipes substitute vodka or isopropyl alcohol for ease. Bay leaf used here is culinary bay (Laurus nobilis), which is widely available and gives a similar aromatic profile. Formulation adapted from The Herbal Apothecary by JJ Pursell (2015).

recipe.batchNotes: Infuse a larger batch and bottle as needed. Keep in a sealed jar during the infusion.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Infuse for two weeks minimum; four weeks for a fuller, more rounded flavour. Strain through a fine cloth before bottling.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a sealed bottle at room temperature. The high alcohol content preserves the splash indefinitely; scent may mellow slightly over the first year.

glossaryTerms.definition: A distilled extract of the Hamamelis virginiana plant, used in skincare as a mild toner and astringent. In aftershave formulas it firms the skin slightly and extends the alcohol base.

content.text: Combine the crumbled bay leaves and lightly crushed allspice in a 200 ml glass jar. Pour the vodka over the spices, seal the jar, and leave in a cool dark place for two to four weeks, shaking once daily.

Strain the infusion through a fine-mesh strainer and then through muslin or a paper coffee filter into a clean jar. Discard the spent spices. Stir in the witch hazel and distilled water. Taste the balance, add more water if the splash feels too sharp, more witch hazel if you want more firmness. Bottle with a funnel.
Pour a small amount into the palm after shaving and pat onto clean, damp skin. The alcohol evaporates quickly; the spiced scent dissipates within a few minutes. Follow with a moisturiser if needed.
Two years in a sealed bottle at room temperature. The high alcohol content is its own preservative.
